bullets.title: Alphabet launches 10-part IG bond sale; hyperscaler CDS spreads widen
bullets.body: Alphabet kicked off a 10-part US dollar investment-grade bond sale, prompting hyperscaler CDS spreads to move wider. Treasuries also fell in the wake of the offering alongside the Warsh report.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh open to September rate hike; sticking with hawkish lean despite market backlash
bullets.body: FT reports Warsh would consider raising rates in September if inflation comes in hot or market expectations for higher borrowing costs increase. Warsh plans to stick with restrictive messaging despite market pushback. Separately, Trump has reportedly spoken repeatedly with Warsh since his confirmation—a departure from recent norms.

bullets.title: TSMC holding ~$1B in Apple A20 Pro SoCs due to DRAM supply bottleneck
bullets.body: TSMC reportedly sitting on approximately $1 billion worth of Apple A20 Pro SoCs that cannot advance to the next production stage due to insufficient DRAM availability. The supply constraint suggests TSMC cannot fulfill Apple orders until DRAM supply normalizes.

bullets.title: WBD Q2: EPS beat, revenue miss; streaming EBITDA +75% YoY
bullets.body: Warner Bros. Discovery posted Q2 EPS of 6¢ vs. estimated loss of 10¢, but revenue came in at $8.72B vs. $9.22B estimate. Streaming adjusted EBITDA surged 75% YoY to $512M; streaming revenue of $3.08B slightly beat the $3.04B estimate. UK CMA also cleared the Paramount/Warner Bros. deal without a Phase 2 review, and Paramount said the deal raises no antitrust concerns in any market.

bullets.title: AI capex/ROI concerns returning as Nasdaq slips on 'AI anxiety'
bullets.body: Bloomberg notes that AI sector concerns about elevated capex, ROI, and circular financing had dissipated but are now back in focus as the market shifts from risk-on to risk-off. Nasdaq futures slipped ~0.6% pre-market. Market Ear also flagged that 'something isn't right beneath the AI rebound.'

bullets.title: META's Muse 1.2 reportedly leapfrogs Google in AI model quality
bullets.body: A fintwit account notes META has 'leapfrogged GOOGL in model quality with Muse 1.2 for many use cases,' calling the achievement surprising given the short timeframe. Separately, one account argues META is now in an even better strategic position than two years ago to execute a 'scorched earth' play leveraging emerging compute and power advantages.

bullets.title: Memory names (WDC/SNDK) sold off despite strong Q2 results—elevated buy-side expectations the culprit
bullets.body: Goldman TMT noted both SanDisk and Western Digital beat on revenue, gross margin, and EPS, yet both traded lower after hours. The issue was 'elevated buy-side expectations going into results, not current quarter performance.'

bullets.title: Bezos sells ~1.2M AMZN shares for ~$346M; Amazon expands GLP-1 same-day delivery
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos disclosed sale of 1,209,649 Amazon shares at $286.41/share for ~$346.5M in proceeds. Separately, Amazon now offers GLP-1 same-day delivery in 3,100+ US cities and plans to expand to ~4,500 cities by end-2026, positioning it to capture growing weight-loss drug delivery demand.

bullets.title: SOXL records near-record MOC buying imbalance (~$8.5B)
bullets.body: The semis ETF SOXL saw a MOC buying imbalance just shy of $8.5B—the sixth-largest in the fund's history and the largest ever when SOXL's market cap was below $25B—signaling significant institutional repositioning into semis.

bullets.title: High-beta momentum crash of July 2026 seen as ongoing; KOSPI down 22% in a month
bullets.body: One macro account maintains that the July 2026 high-beta momentum crash is 'not yet' over, with no clear reversal signal. South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.6% overnight, is down 22% in the last month, and off 31% from its bubble peak—with the author maintaining a short position.

bullets.title: SPX 0DTE volume dropped to 56% vs. typical 60-70%—derivatives positioning shifting
bullets.body: SPX 0DTE flows typically represent 60-70% of volume, but dropped to 56% over the last two sessions. Chunky 0DTE positions were liquidated Monday when 0DTE vol was underpriced, accompanied by a massive surge in non-0DTE volume—signaling a shift in derivatives market structure.

bullets.title: BofA raises 2027 uranium price forecast to $130/lb (~52% upside)
bullets.body: BofA lifted its 2027 uranium price forecast to $130/lb, implying ~52% upside from current spot. The bullish view is driven by tight supply and utility contract coverage declining to 48% from 56% last year, alongside growing nuclear investment demand.

bullets.title: Hormuz deal potentially days away; Oman-Iran corridor statement imminent
bullets.body: Tehran and Muscat have reportedly reached broad agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with a deal announcement potentially within days. A proposed 60-day transit corridor agreement still requires Iran security council approval. Oman and Iran are expected to issue a joint statement imminently.

bullets.title: UBER: 46% market underperformance despite Q2 gross bookings +24% to $58B
bullets.body: Uber has underperformed the market by 46% over the last 12 months despite strong Q2 2026 results: gross bookings +24% YoY to $58B, trips +18% to 3.9B, adjusted EBITDA +33% to $2.82B, and trailing 12-month FCF reaching $10.5B.

bullets.title: Long U / Short APP trade flagged; Unity Q2 shows most positive survey results ever
bullets.body: One fintwit account put on a 'Long $U Short $APP' pair trade. A separate preview note flagged that Unity's D28 IAA is driving clear acceleration in vector growth with the most positive survey results ever recorded for the company.

bullets.title: Invesco: Fed is not behind the curve; neutral rate at 3.5%-4.0%
bullets.body: Invesco argues the Fed is not behind the curve, estimating the neutral rate at 3.5%-4.0%—aligned with the current 3.50%-3.75% policy range. This counters recent market debate suggesting policy is too restrictive or too loose.

bullets.title: Saudi Aramco cuts September Arab Light OSP to Asia by 50¢/bbl
bullets.body: Saudi Aramco set September Arab Light crude at a $2/bbl discount to the regional benchmark for Asia, cutting prices by 50¢/bbl month-over-month. Arab Light for NW Europe was set at -$2.15/bbl to ICE Brent.

bullets.title: INTC: Diamond Rapids 'Xeon 7' surfaces with 32 cores and 240MB L3 cache
bullets.body: Intel's next-gen Diamond Rapids Xeon 7 CPU has surfaced featuring 32 cores and a 240MB L3 cache on the Oakstream platform, suggesting Intel is advancing its server CPU roadmap.

bullets.title: SMR/nuclear positioned as AI infrastructure winners amid power demand surge
bullets.body: Commentary highlights small modular reactor companies as positioned to benefit from the data center power demand cycle, with nuclear re-emerging as a strategic priority for AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: CEG Q2: EPS beat at $2.55 vs. $2.35 est; revenue misses at $7.5B vs. $7.7B est
bullets.body: Constellation Energy reported Q2 EPS of $2.55, beating the $2.35 estimate, but revenue of $7.5B missed the $7.7B consensus.
